title: introduce-stream-sink-and-graceful-auth-timeout-for-cross-sdk-parity
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Added StreamSink abstraction and graceful auth timeout / reauth flow to go SDK. Aligns behavior with Python/TypeScript SDKs. Bumped go SDK version to v0.21.0. Backwards compatible with current stream consumer code with minor adapter helper.
description:
Context: This PR implements a StreamSink abstraction in the Go SDK and updates the auth/reauth timeout behavior for streaming clients to match the ergonomics of the Python and TypeScript SDKs. Motivation: customers hit two cross-language inconsistencies during the recent canary: (1) long-running stream consumers could lose progress when token refresh raced with stream IO, and (2) there was no simple consumer-facing sink abstraction equivalent to the TS/Py "sink" helpers. Both made porting production consumers between languages error-prone.

What changed (high-level):
- Added sdk/go/stream/sink.go: StreamSink is an ergonomic helper that accepts a context, writes messages into an internal buffer, and exposes a single Close/Err semantics for graceful shutdowns. It supports backpressure hints for the runtime.
- Implemented a conservative auth timeout and reauth handshake in sdk/go/auth/refresh.go used by streaming transports. The flow ensures an in-flight stream write won't be interrupted mid-message when a token refresh occurs; refresh happens proactively with a configurable prefetch window and a short graceful timeout to drain pending writes.
- Centralized retry/backoff helpers in sdk/go/transport/retry.go and aligned parameters with TS/Py defaults (base=100ms, max=3s, jitter).
- Added internal/compat/stream_adapter.go to provide a thin adapter so existing consumer code continues to work; this keeps backward compatibility while encouraging migration to StreamSink.
- Tests: added unit tests for sink and retry logic, and an integration test that simulates concurrent token refresh + stream writes (auth/refresh_integration_test.go).
- Docs: sdk-go streaming.md and examples showing recommended migration paths.
- Version bump: go SDK bumped to v0.21.0 (sdk/go/version.go, changelog).

Commits (summary):
- a1f3d7d: feat(stream): add StreamSink abstraction and basic tests
- b27c8a2: feat(auth): proactive refresh prefetch and graceful timeout for streams
- c3b9ea1: chore: align retry defaults with ts/py and add jitter util
- d4aa1ff: test: integration test for refresh+write race and fix flapper
- e5f7b9c: docs: streaming guide and example update
- f6123ab: ci: add flaky toleration on integration job; lint fixes

Files changed (high-level): see changed_files field above. Changes are focused to SDK surface (stream, auth, transport), docs and examples. There are no server-side changes.

Review timeline & conversation (condensed):
- Diego: requested clearer guarantees in the README about exactly when the sink returns Err after Close; suggested making the prefetch window configurable.
- Author (Aisha): replied with a design note and added prefetch config with a sensible default (30s) and documented behavior.
- Connor: asked for an additional unit test to reproduce a token-refresh-with-large-queued-messages race; test added and fixed a minor locking bug.
- Maya: requested docs/sample for migrating existing consumers; author added an examples/stream-reconnect/go and expanded docs.
- CI initially failed on lint (go vet and staticcheck) and a flaky integration run; author addressed lint and made integration test more deterministic by adding deterministic timing hooks.
- Final status: reviewers approved and Diego left an approval with comments.

CI details: initial run (linux, macos, windows) - lint failed; subsequent run passed. Integration job retried twice due to resource flakiness on the first run, passed on second. e2e matrix summary: unit tests 100% pass, integration tests 3/3 pass on final.

Compatibility & migration notes:
- Existing streaming consumers that call client.StreamConsume(context, handler) continue to work via internal stream_adapter; the adapter is a thin shim that maps old callbacks to the new StreamSink semantics. Migration recommendation is to adopt StreamSink for simpler shutdown/error semantics and to gain built-in reauth safety.
- Config knobs: "AuthPrefetchWindow" (default "30s"), "AuthGracefulTimeout" (default "3s"), and retry params are exposed on client.Options. These match TS/Py defaults and will be part of the public compatibility matrix in the SDK docs.

Backports & follow-ups:
- A small backport to the 0.20.x branch will be prepared if support tickets reference the race; backport ticket created (SUP-4421).
- Coordinated TS and Python PRs were opened to mirror the same ergonomics; see related: github.com/redwood/redwood-sdk-typescript/pull/1123 and github.com/redwood/redwood-sdk-python/pull/789 (links present in the repo comments).

Merge: PR was squashed and merged into main on 2026-03-05 after approvals. Change is non-breaking and shipped under feature flag (default-on) for a short ramp period.

Notes for release: include the streaming migration snippet in the SDK release notes and call out the reauth knob defaults so infra teams can tune for low-latency long-running streams.
notes: Coordinated with TS/Py SDK owners for parity
